chapter_scope: v03-c01 and v03-c02 only; remaining volume chapters and assessment remain planned
review_type: Author analytic, numerical and instructional review; not independent certification

reviewed.reasoning: Reviewed probability-space/event definitions, countable axioms and derived complement/monotonicity/union/intersection bounds; counting multiplicity and factorial/combinatorial proofs; sampling support and replacement mechanisms; pairwise versus mutual independence and complement factorization; normalized countable laws and probability continuity. Conditional chapter derives the conditioned measure, chain/total probability and Bayes normalizations; distinguishes null-event ratios from specified model likelihoods; odds endpoints, sequential history-dependent evidence, latent-quality and selection dependence, stopping/reporting likelihood and sensitivity versus credible intervals.
reviewed.arithmetic: Exact weighted tables and all atom probabilities; exhaustive subset and ordered-record enumeration for both archive mechanisms; analyst-role/committee enumeration; exact geometric sums with remainder; joint census tables, posterior and odds checks; explicit latent-quality/test state laws and prediction extension; duplicated-report and selected-bit laws; stopping sequences; finite-difference prior-response derivative; downloaded exact-fraction lab cross-check.
reviewed.solutions: All sixteen prompts independently recomputed, including invalid input table, higher-order independence, reversed conditionals, normalized three-hypothesis evidence, ordered versus aggregate observations, false-positive sensitivity threshold and stopping-time evidence. All eight exercise solutions in each chapter match their prompts.
reviewed.instruction: Defines outcomes/events, power set and sigma-algebra at an introductory level; full measure/integration construction remains Chapter 12. Counting multiplicity and sampling law are explained before formula use. Conditional evidence and reference group are distinguished before numerical updating. No probability estimation, causal effect, optimal decision or actual October observation is claimed from synthetic models.
reviewed.sources: Four method-specific official MIT PDFs and the Harvard course About route retrieved. Uses are documented as further-study/method routes, with original chapter prose and problems.
reviewed.structure: Each chapter contains two worked examples, eight exercises with complete solutions, hypothesis/boundary checks, teach-back, delayed checks, sources and an optional offline standard-library laboratory.

corrections: Made the countable first-success record space explicitly allow a never-success outcome of probability zero.
Explicitly distinguished undefined elementary conditioning on a zero-prior event from a separately specified hypothetical model likelihood.
Specified that replacing files permits repetition but requires fresh independent randomization to justify independent draws.
limitations: No independent human reviewer or learner trial.
